description: Bright green plates with black seams, alive-looking. Its creature is still somewhere in the deep wood.
lore: Four or five come in a season, always off the deep-wood roads, always the same stone: bright green plates, seams gone nearly black, the whole of it wet-looking in a dry hand. It sells the day it lands. Everything in that wood bites and most of it is worse an hour later, and a piece that finishes a poison in half the time it would have taken is worth a hundred and fifteen gold to anyone who works in there, and more to anyone who has been carried out of it once already.

What the trade cannot do with it is the ordinary thing. [[lore/the_hard_pieces|People who crack shapes for a living]] keep books — the shape, the ground, the morning, who swung — because that is how they are paid and how they settle arguments, and every other stone on a bench can be walked back along one of them. This one is in nobody's book. Every seller of one bought it from a seller; run the chain back and it goes three or four hands and stops — at a road, at a fire that is not kept any more, at a man who has moved on and cannot be produced.

So the sellers say its creature is still out there in the deep wood, and it is a good line, and it costs nothing, and it may well be true. It is also an answer to a question that was not asked. Where the creature is has never been the difficulty here. Where the stones are coming from is.
gm_notes: Unbound stone: no creature invented and none asserted. The cold question is deliberately supply, not location — the crackers' books are the mechanism that makes the gap visible, and the shipped sellers' line is left standing as the comfortable answer it is. Do not tie this to the cave; the point is that it is unaccounted for, not that it is accounted for elsewhere.
